key_insight: A model-based reinforcement learning policy can autonomously steer droplets through complex labyrinth geometries using limited real-world data and no explicit droplet physics model.
engineering_relevance: This enables more reliable, adaptive control for lab-on-a-chip and droplet microfluidic systems where nonlinear pinning and hysteresis defeat classical trajectory planning.
method: Thin silicone oil film reduces contact-line pinning
Two-axis platform tilt provides gravity-driven actuation
Overhead camera supplies real-time droplet tracking for offline-trained policy learning
evidence_signal: The learned policy successfully navigated straight, right-angle, curved-arc, and outside-corner paths, including zero-shot transfer to harder geometries and improved performance with only one-fifth of the training data.
watch_item: The controller operates under partial observability, so hidden film thickness, contact-angle dynamics, and droplet deformation may limit robustness outside the tested platform conditions.
paper_title: Autonomous Droplet Navigation via Model-Based Reinforcement Learning
